We should build what makes Arcwright unique, use other tech as part of our stack, and replace third parties only when we need features they don't offer, they get too expensive, or we want to build our own custome version for a strong purpose." Standing instruction: "never hesitate to say that the purpose of Arcwright is already solved broadly with existing technology." Budget, in his words: "let's start with free and keep max $50 as needed." Nothing is installed, signed up for or bought without founder approval. He is open to writer-controlled branching story tools and visual story editors, and to Unity or Unreal if necessary. Full rule: ADR-0026. Full target stack with verified licences and prices: docs/architecture/02-technology-stack.md section 2.11.

Decision: D-115 Play data is captured at engine level in one game-agnostic shape, for every game built on Arcwright
Rationale: Founder decision during the reset interview. Founder's words: "Data is key and capturing gameplay at the engine level should enable us to improve nightcap and any other game built. Improve game play, characters, stories, plot, arcs, pace, etc." and "The data and learning should be useful for all games that use Arcwright." Every session records the same generic facts: story units entered and left, who learned what and from whom, what participants chose from what was offered, what characters said, tension against the author's target, and cost. Game-specific words in records become game configuration. Analysis, a graph database add-on and any model training wait for session volume and, for training, player consent; architecture principle 7 still excludes foundation-model training at MVP. Tasks: AW-304 (records), AW-314 (story library experiment).

Decision: D-116 Players wanting one more game is a stated Nightcap goal for every session
Rationale: Founder decision during the reset interview. Founder's words: "people should want to play one more time at the end of each game!" The goal was not stated anywhere in the GDD, and replay intent was weak in the v2.2 paper test. Wanting to play again is measured in session 1 with the approved pass bar (at least half answer yes). Being able to play again needs a second case; the route is a human defining truth and structure with AI writing within it, which the founder confirmed ("AI can write parts of stories once the human defines certain parts") and which matches architecture principles 2 and 3. Adding the goal to the GDD needs the founder's approval of the wording: AW-307.

Decision: D-117 Connect a story-writing tool before session 1; write the second case in it; compare the two
Rationale: Founder decision during the reset interview. Founder's words: "After building the case and before session 1, I want to integrate with story tools to have a back up for me to build a story with those tools ahead of session 2. I.e. session 1 with the in progress case used, we learn from that to build a new case with the new tools and a/b test them." The first case is not converted mid-flight. Existing story tools write branching scenes and do not model who knows what or fair routes to a truth, so the work is an importer into Arcwright's format, not a replacement. The comparison is two different cases, so it shows which tool is easier to write in more clearly than which players prefer. If build sessions run short the importer is the last item cut. Task: AW-306.

Decision: D-118 Work is delivered in three lanes; the rebuild uses three combined specs
Rationale: Founder decision. The proposal: small fixes and documentation need a short plan; the Nightcap rebuild needs three combined specs (engine spine, screens, endgame) instead of about twelve separate spec approvals; anything touching the database, several engine modules, prompts or new dependencies always needs founder approval under the hard rules in AGENTS.md. Founder's answer: "Im fine with this, but we are doing spec-driven development." Spec-driven development stays the method; the change is the size of the unit approved. Recorded in docs/roadmap/operations/working-model.md. Task: AW-302.

Decision: D-126 A mini-game win gives the top-ranked one extra investigation (spec 0093, Q1)

Decision: D-127 Working rule: move fast, stay open to change, prefer choices that are cheap to undo
Rationale: Founder instruction, 2026-11-16, in session. Founder's words: "Lets move quickly and be open to change if they ont turn out to be the best solution. We need to be quick, nimble, flexible, and open to trying different things safely. remember that." and "Be smart. Make thoughtful decisions that dont remove flexibility." Scribe's reading, labelled as interpretation: (1) An approved spec is the current best plan, not a fixed contract. (2) A session that finds a better way says so on the task's issue with a recommendation; it neither builds the worse thing in silence nor changes the plan in silence. The change is recorded in the spec the same day. (3) Between two designs that both work, pick the one that is cheaper to change later: values in configuration files, old paths left untouched, no table change unless needed. (4) Safely means the hard rules in AGENTS.md and plan approval before code still apply, and experiments are small and reversible. This rule does not lift the tooling freeze (D-110, D-111) or any approval gate.

Decision: D-128 Nightcap's screens protect the feeling "I outsmarted you" first
Rationale: Founder interview answer, 2026-11-16, in session. Question asked: "Picture the best five minutes of session 1 at your house. Which feeling must the screens protect first when two of these pull against each other?" The founder chose "I outsmarted you (Recommended)", described as: players feel clever and competitive; the best moment is one player's theory landing and the others groaning that they missed it; screens favour private thinking time on the phone and a big public reveal on the TV. Evidence note: this is a choice among options written by the session, not the founder's own wording. The open question asked for his own words, and he may still restate it. It matches the player fantasy in docs/gdd/nightcap/00-governance/02-current-design-state.md. Scribe's reading for the screens spec (AW-302): where private thinking on the phone and shared party energy on the TV compete for time or space, private thinking and the public reveal win. The other three feelings stay wanted and rank below it. Adds no scope.

Decision: D-129 Arcwright's first outside creator is a writer who cannot code
Rationale: Founder interview answer, 2026-11-16, in session. Question asked: "Who is the first person outside your own work that the engine should serve? This decides what gets built after session 1, not before it." Four options were offered: a writer who cannot code; an indie game developer; a company event designer; nobody yet. The founder chose the writer (the session's recommendation), described as: a mystery or tabletop writer who authors a new Nightcap case in the story tool, with no engineer. Why: it is the cheapest real test, it reuses everything built for session 1, and it proves a stranger can write a playable story from the docs alone. Known limit: it does not prove the engine runs a second kind of game. Scribe's reading: after session 1, the authoring path (the adopted story tool of D-122, its importer AW-306, the case format and fairness report of spec 0093, and author-facing docs) comes before a public API, an SDK for outside developers, or an enterprise arc. Not decided: who the person is, when, and what evidence justifies opening the platform; that half of the open question stays open. Adds no build scope before session 1 and changes no roadmap task.

Decision: D-130 The TV reads the round's public status without signing in, for the thin version

Reading it needs the game's ID, a random identifier. Explained to the founder before approval: anyone holding the game's link can read what the TV in the room already shows; the alternative was a TV sign-in paired by the host, more build work now. Scope: the thin version (D-112). Revisit with real sign-in (AW-269). Relates to Part M1 of the draft screens spec 0095 (room view without sign-in). Approves an auth exception under the AGENTS.md hard rule on auth; adds no other scope.

Decision: D-133 Host controls live in a Start menu on the phones; every player can pause; the first to join is host and can hand it on (spec 0095, Q1)
Rationale: Founder answer to Q1 of the draft screens spec, 2026-11-18, in the orchestrator session. Question asked: where do the host's controls live? Options offered: (1) a strip in a corner of the TV page, the spec's recommendation; (2) a separate host page on a phone; (3) both. Founder's words: "A separate host page on a phone. Easy to reach from the sofa. The catch: one more link, and if you're also playing you switch tabs or use a second phone. Just desinate a host that has the controls on their phone or add game pause on the phones similar to how video game controllers have a start menu". Asked who may pause, he chose "Everyone can pause (Recommended)". Asked to confirm the summary, he replied "Yes, but host can be reassigned by the first to join too. Also there should be a start menu and settings on the phones for everyone and the start menu actions depend on if youre host or regular player. The rest looks correct". What was decided: no host controls on the TV and no separate host link. Every phone has a Start menu with Pause, Resume and Settings. The host's Start menu also has Start game, Move on, mini-game Resolve and Cancel, End game, and handing the host role to another seated player. The host is the first player to join. The host's menu shows only what the whole room may see. Scribe's reading, labelled as interpretation: "host can be reassigned by the first to join" is read as the current host may hand the role on. Not decided (proposals for the AW-330 and AW-331 plans): what Settings holds; whether anyone may resume another player's pause; what happens to the host role when the host's phone drops. Does not approve: spec 0095 as a whole, which is still a draft; any plan or code. The sign-in changes (a player may pause; the host role moves to a player's seat) are an AGENTS.md hard rule and need explicit approval in AW-331's plan. Recorded in docs/specs/0095-screens-for-the-thin-version.md, "Q1 Answered", and on issue #355.

Decision: D-136 A round may hold more than one mini-game up to a flexible cap; solo mini-games can be found through investigation; no mechanic repeats in a playthrough (amends D-113; spec 0095 Q4)
Rationale: Founder answers to Q4 of the draft screens spec, 18 to 19 November 2026, in the orchestrator session. Founder's words, in order: "Wrappers can change the style/aesthetic of the game to match the story, but it doesnt change the mechanic, so playing the same game mechanic multiple times in one playthrough of the game seems like what we wouldnt want to do." Then "I want the best number fo mini-games to fit a playthrough, not just trying to force in whats possible given our current mini-game inventory. I would rather create more mini-games to make it correct than adjusted for the test." Then "Dont get to hung up on trying to measure the amount of time to play the game. We will find that out when we test and adjust from there based on player experience and feedback." And "Im not married to 1 mini-game per round either. Some games could be played faster than others. There should be a cap per round, but it should be flexible and not exclusively 1. Some mini-games could also only be for one player if they stumble onto something other players havent." Confirmed summary, chosen "Yes, record it (Recommended)": (1) a round may hold more than one mini-game, up to a cap set per round in Nightcap's arc file; one per round is no longer the rule, amending D-113's "ending in a story-wrapped mini-game"; (2) solo mini-games: an investigation can lead one player into a private mini-game only they found, built for session 1; (3) no repeated mechanic in one playthrough, because a wrapper changes the look, not the mechanic; mechanics are built new or adapted for 2 to 4 players rather than fitting the game to today's inventory; the number of mechanics follows from design and testing, not from a time estimate. Prior art the founder endorsed: It Takes Two's director used most mechanics for one scene only, because repetition is why story games go unfinished (reset audit, section 3). Boundary: rounds, caps and which mini-games run are Nightcap configuration; the Arcwright engine only runs an ordered list of bindings on a beat and starts a mini-game when an authored trigger fires (AGENTS.md principle 1, D-113's engine half stands). Tasks: AW-344 (several mini-games per round, engine), AW-345 (solo mini-game found through investigation, engine and design), AW-337 rewritten (design and build the mechanics set). Each plan needs founder approval. Recorded in docs/specs/0095-screens-for-the-thin-version.md, "Q4 Answered", and on issue #355.

Decision: D-138 Last Call theory: fill a short written account with pieces you found, pin one proof; the winner's proof is shown at the Verdict (spec 0095 Q5; amends spec 0094 Part J)
Rationale: Founder answer to Q5 of the draft screens spec, 19 November 2026, in the orchestrator session. Asked about Q5, the founder first asked "What are the bust versions we thought through in the GDD?", then "Knowing what you know about how to creat amazing, fun, engaging, world class, and billion dollar games, is this the best way to do it? Do you have other suggestions?", then "What would be the best version for the dysfunctional detective agency idea I had?", then "I'm feeling better, but what does the gameplay look like? We can skip the skinning for right now and add it to part of the detective agency strategy." Shown a walkthrough, he answered the question "Lock this Last Call gameplay (fill the story from your own pieces, pin one proof, lock; the winner's proof shown on the TV at the Verdict; the proof does not change who wins)?" with "Lock it (Recommended)". The option he chose said: "Spec 0094's Verdict change is approved by this answer." What was decided: The Last Call theory is Structured Reconstruction (the GDD's V1, spec 0092 Q3) presented as a short written account. (1) The case writer writes a short account of what happened with blanks; each blank is one of the case's solution slots (spec 0093 Part A), in the case's order. The player fills each blank by tapping pieces they hold themselves, true and misleading alike, in an order that never hints at the answer (spec 0094 Part G is otherwise unchanged). (2) The player also pins one held piece as their proof. The proof does not change who wins: the theory check and the winner rule (spec 0094 Parts H and I) are unchanged. (3) At the Verdict the TV shows the winner's proof with their name; nobody else's proof is shown publicly. Each phone shows its own blanks marked right or wrong only after the TV's Verdict (D-128). (4) The detective-agency wording (case report, Exhibit A, performance reviews, the side guess) is not part of this decision; it moves to the detective agency strategy, AW-319. Prior art considered (GameGene records): The Case of the Golden Idol judges a completed written account, not a name; Ace Attorney's single moment of presenting the decisive evidence; Return of the Obra Dinn and Golden Idol's partial-correctness feedback was rejected because the GDD forbids incremental correctness feedback. Changes: the case format gains an account text around the solution slots and the theory form gains one proof field (AW-326); the Verdict shows the winner's proof (AW-327); the case writer writes the account (AW-305). No table change, no model call. Does not approve spec 0095 as a whole. Recorded in docs/specs/0095-screens-for-the-thin-version.md "Q5 Answered", docs/specs/0094-endgame-for-the-thin-version.md, and issue #355.

Decision: D-143 Mini-games are fun first: skinned to the story when natural, openly a game when not; the same mechanic can run solo, as a pair or as a group (amends D-113 and D-136 wording; changes the GDD Diegetic Action Rule)
Rationale: Founder answer, 19 November 2026, in the orchestrator session, during the AW-337 mechanics interview. Founder's words: "they don't have to always be perfectlyseemless in the story. That's nice to have, but they don't have to always feel like they are perfectly part of the story. They can be skinned to fit the story." "lock picking mini game could be a solo game if a person finds a locked box as a clue alonenor a group game if every has access or a pair game if two find it at the same time." "It would be tedious to always try to make the story conform to account for mini-games and risk feeling jarring. When natural.and appropriate, do it. When not, don't pretend to be part of the story if it's just for fun. We should expect people to know that it's a game  and breaking the fourth wall is part of it. I say all this because the game must be fun first and foremost." Confirmed summary, chosen "Yes, record all thrree": fun comes first; a mini-game is skinned to the story when that is natural, and otherwise is openly a game; breaking the fourth wall is fine; the link back to the story is its reward (one extra investigation, D-126) and the host's line after it, not a forced fiction; the same mechanic can run solo, as a pair or as a group depending on how players reach it. Amends the "story-wrapped" wording of D-113 and D-136. Also changes the GDD's Diegetic Action Rule (docs/gdd/nightcap/01-authoritative-gdd/04-minigame-competitive-pulse.md: a major minigame "should normally feel like something the detective is actually doing in the fiction"); the orchestrator raised that after the summary was confirmed; asked whether to update the GDD rule to match, keeping the part that tells players what they are doing and what is at stake, the founder answered Yes, update it. The rule is now the Story Fit Rule on that page, and the decision ledger line is changed to match. Open, not decided: how a pair mini-game starts when two players reach the same thing, and whether a mechanic used as one player's solo mini-game counts against the no-repeat rule (D-136).

Decision: D-147 A beat's mini-games are slots in the arc file, and an adaptive beat picks each game by one fixed rule: arc-file order, filtered by the player count the game declares and by no-repeat mechanics, first one left
Rationale: Founder approval, 19 November 2026, in the AW-344 build session, answering "Is 'arc-file order, filtered by player count and no-repeat, first one left' the picking rule you want?" with "Yes, that rule". Plan posted on issue #427 (AW-344). Meaning as recorded: (1) a beat lists as many mini_game phases as it allows; each is a slot with its own clock and its own run, and that number is the cap, read from the arc file; zero is allowed. (2) A beat's mini_game_pick is listed (default, today's behaviour: slot N runs binding N) or fitting (the beat's bindings are a pool; each slot runs the first binding, in arc-file order, whose package declares a player range that holds the session's player count (D-142) and whose mechanic has not been started in this session (D-136); none left skips the slot, records it and tells the host). (3) A run counts as played once it has started, even if it timed out or was cancelled. (4) Rules decide, never AI. Answers the open question raised by D-145. Alternatives not chosen: host picks; seeded random; player-type cohort (D-146), which can be added later as one more filter in AW-346. Not approved here: a race mini-game running during Last Call (the commit phase); it waits on AW-346.

Decision: D-155 Opt-in mini-game result hold with a privacy-safe, phase-bound result read
Rationale: Founder decision in the AW-351 build session on PR #472 and issue #457. Asked how a mini-game result should fit the flow, the founder selected "Pause for results (Recommended): show the result, then continue when players are ready or a clock expires." After reviewing the proposed completed-result design, including the opt-in arc phase setting, cross-module work, public-data allowlist and a 15-second adjustable playtest starting value, the founder answered "Approve!" The engine owns the hold and advances on all eligible players ready, the deadline or host move-on. A result read must identify the run bound to the current session, beat and phase visit and exclude private submissions, prompts, raw outcomes, behavioral signals and private rewards. Existing phases without the setting keep immediate advance. This amends the immediate-advance rule in spec 0093 Part E for opted-in holds; that spec must be reconciled before implementation. The implementation plan requires separate founder approval. The 15-second value is a playtest starting point, not a proven ideal. Solo-game visibility remains for AW-345; this decision does not approve broadcasting solo results. Founder subsequently allowed a narrowly scoped exception to the earlier prohibition on editing this log solely to record this decision.
